accepted.s: Who wrote the book *The Rise and Growth of Economic Nationalism in India*?
accepted.x: *The Rise and Growth of Economic Nationalism in India* was written by Bipan Chandra and was published in 1966.
accepted.tq: Use direct author–book recall and distinguish modern works from colonial-period economic critiques.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Essays on Indian Economics — M.G. Ranade
Economic History of India — Bipan Chandra
Some Economic Aspects of British Rule in India — R.C. Dutt
The Rise and Growth of Economic Nationalism in India — G. Subramania Iyer
accepted.x: M.G. Ranade wrote *Essays on Indian Economics*. The other works were authored by R.C. Dutt, G. Subramania Iyer and Bipan Chandra respectively.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure author–book pair and eliminate swapped authors.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the publication years of economic works:
1. *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India* was published in 1901.
2. *Essays on Indian Economics* was published in 1898.
3. *Some Economic Aspects of British Rule in India* was published in 1903.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: Naoroji’s work dates to 1901, Ranade’s to 1898 and G. Subramania Iyer’s to 1903.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical statement independently before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s: *India Today* was written by whom?
accepted.x: *India Today* was written by Rajani Palme Dutt.
accepted.tq: Test exact author–title association without confusing R.C. Dutt with Rajani Palme Dutt.

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a channel through which Britain drained India’s wealth?
accepted.x: The drain operated through Home Charges, salaries and pensions, unequal trade and British monopoly. Expansion of indigenous industrial ownership was not a channel of the drain.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the economic relationship described by the drain theory.

accepted.s: The origin of the drain theory was linked by the economic critics to which development?
o: The devastation following the suppression of the Revolt of 1857
The introduction of dyarchy in the provinces
The formation of the Muslim League in 1906
accepted.x: The origin of the drain theory was linked to the economic devastation that followed the suppression of the Revolt of 1857.
accepted.tq: Connect the theory with its historical context rather than with a later nationalist event.

accepted.s: Who described Britain as “bleeding India white”?
accepted.x: Dadabhai Naoroji used the expression “bleeding India white” while explaining the colonial economic drain.
accepted.tq: Use quotation–person association as a direct recall item.

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a major economic demand of the Moderates?
accepted.x: The Moderates demanded cuts in military expenditure, along with lower land revenue, abolition of the salt tax and tariff protection for Indian industries.
accepted.tq: Reject the option that reverses a stated demand.

accepted.s: The economic demands of the Moderates were later adopted substantially by which of the following?
o: The British Conservative Party and the Muslim League alone
The princely states and the East India Company
The Governor-General and the Secretary of State alone
accepted.x: The economic demands first pressed by the Moderates were later adopted by the Extremists and Mahatma Gandhi.
accepted.tq: Test the historical continuity of a political demand across phases of nationalism.

accepted.s: The Servants of India Society was founded at which place and on which date?
accepted.x: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society at Poona on 12 June 1905.
accepted.tq: Combine place and date to avoid selecting a nearby nationalist-event date.
accepted.sec: Gokhale - Servants of India Society, political guru relationships  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What was the principal purpose of the Servants of India Society?
o: To promote British monopoly over Indian trade
To organise armed revolutionary groups abroad
To train dedicated national workers and responsible leaders
accepted.x: The Society trained dedicated public workers and responsible leaders and promoted India’s interests through constitutional means.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution’s function from the activity most closely matching its stated objectives.
accepted.sec: Gokhale - Servants of India Society, political guru relationships  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was Gopal Krishna Gokhale’s own guru?
accepted.x: M.G. Ranade was Gokhale’s political and intellectual guru.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of a mentor relationship rather than merely recognising both names.
accepted.sec: Gokhale - Servants of India Society, political guru relationships  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Dadabhai Naoroji in chronological order:
A. Foundation of the East India Association
B. Naoroji’s presidency of the Calcutta Congress
C. Naoroji’s presidency of the Lahore Congress
D. Naoroji’s election to the British House of Commons
accepted.x: The correct sequence is East India Association (1866), Lahore Congress presidency (1893), election to the House of Commons (1892), and Calcutta Congress presidency (1906). Therefore, chronologically the sequence should be A, D, C, B only if the given labels are interpreted by dates? Actually, the correct order is A, D, C, B is inconsistent because Lahore 1893 follows Commons 1892; the listed events are A (1866), D (1892), C (1893), B (1906).
accepted.tq: Place the dated events first and check each adjacent pair carefully.
accepted.sec: Dadabhai Naoroji - presidencies, title, British Parliament, drain theory  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents Dadabhai Naoroji’s three presidencies of the Indian National Congress?
accepted.x: Naoroji presided over the Congress at Calcutta in 1886, Lahore in 1893 and Calcutta again in 1906.
accepted.tq: Use the repeated city and the middle Lahore session to identify the complete sequence.
accepted.sec: Dadabhai Naoroji - presidencies, title, British Parliament, drain theory  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At which Congress session did Swaraj become the goal under Dadabhai Naoroji’s presidency?
accepted.x: Swaraj became the goal at the Calcutta Congress session of 1906 presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji.
accepted.tq: Pair the resolution with the correct session rather than with Naoroji’s earlier presidencies.
accepted.sec: Dadabhai Naoroji - presidencies, title, British Parliament, drain theory  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: R.C. Dutt — *Rise of the Maratha Power*
accepted.x: Surendranath Banerjee wrote *A Nation in Making*. *The Bengalee* was associated with Banerjee, *Rise of the Maratha Power* with Ranade, and *Economic History of India* with R.C. Dutt.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure book–leader pair and identify swapped associations.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes M.G. Ranade?
o: Founder of the Madras Mahajana Sabha and *The Hindu*
Judge, economist and social reformer associated with the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha
First president of the Indian National Congress at Bombay in 1885
Economic historian of the ICS associated with the Lucknow Congress of 1899
accepted.x: M.G. Ranade was a judge, economist and social reformer associated with the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha. The other descriptions refer to R.C. Dutt, G. Subramania Iyer and W.C. Bonnerjee.
accepted.tq: Use the wrong-person-with-deed trap by separating overlapping biographies.

accepted.s: Who among the following presided over the Indian National Congress at Lucknow in 1899?
accepted.x: R.C. Dutt presided over the Lucknow session of the Indian National Congress in 1899.
accepted.tq: Link the leader with the specific Congress session and year.

accepted.s: G. Subramania Iyer was associated with the founding of which pair of newspapers?
accepted.x: G. Subramania Iyer founded *The Hindu* and *Swadesamitran* and was associated with the Madras Mahajana Sabha.
accepted.tq: Match the leader with both newspaper associations rather than one isolated title.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Dinshaw Wacha — First Muslim INC president
Badruddin Tyabji — INC president at Calcutta in 1901
G. Subramania Iyer — INC president at Lucknow in 1899
accepted.x: W.C. Bonnerjee was the first president of the Indian National Congress. Badruddin Tyabji was the first Muslim INC president, while Dinshaw Wacha presided at Calcutta in 1901 and R.C. Dutt at Lucknow in 1899.
accepted.tq: Use the title and session traps to reject swapped Congress presidencies.

accepted.s: Who among the following was associated with the statement “no taxation without representation”?
accepted.x: Madan Mohan Malaviya was associated with the statement “no taxation without representation.”
accepted.tq: Match the quoted political principle with its associated leader.

accepted.s: P. Anandacharlu served as secretary of which organisation in 1884?
accepted.x: P. Anandacharlu was the secretary of the Madras Mahajana Sabha in 1884.
accepted.tq: Distinguish similarly named regional political associations by office and year.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders in the early Congress - sessions presided  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was associated with *Vaijayanti* and *People’s Magazine*?
accepted.x: Nyapathi Subbarao founded the monthly *Vaijayanti* and edited *People’s Magazine*.
accepted.tq: Match the publications with the correct Andhra Congress figure.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders in the early Congress - sessions presided  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following titles were associated with Nyapathi Subbarao?
1. Rajabahadur
2. Padyavinoda
3. Rashtraguru
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Nyapathi Subbarao was associated with the titles Rajabahadur and Padyavinoda. Rashtraguru was the title of Surendranath Banerjee.
accepted.tq: Separate the correct titles from a famous title belonging to another leader.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders in the early Congress - sessions presided  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT listed among the Andhra delegates who attended the first session of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
accepted.x: P. Rangaiah Naidu, Gutti Kesava Pillai and Venkata Subbarayudu were listed among the other Andhra delegates to the first session. Konda Venkatappayya came to prominence among Andhra Moderates after 1908.
accepted.tq: Use the date boundary to identify the later figure among early delegates.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders in the early Congress - sessions presided  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was described as the “Gokhale of South India”?
accepted.x: Mocherla Ramachandra Rao was described as the “Gokhale of South India.”
accepted.tq: Match the sobriquet with the correct regional nationalist leader.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders in the early Congress - sessions presided  [APPSC]

accepted.s: After 1908, which pair of Andhra Moderates came to the fore after the Extremists were crushed?
o: Gutti Kesava Pillai and Venkata Subbarayudu
Mocherla Ramachandra Rao and P. Rangaiah Naidu
accepted.x: After 1908, Konda Venkatappayya and B.N. Sarma came to the forefront among the Andhra Moderates.
accepted.tq: Use the chronological marker to distinguish the post-1908 leadership from the first-session delegates.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders in the early Congress - sessions presided  [APPSC]
